issues.t: Horn works only some of the time (recall)
issues.sym: The horn sounds weakly, cuts out, or does not sound at all when pressed.
issues.why: A poor ground connection in the horn circuit stops current from reaching the horn reliably.
issues.next: Have a dealer check whether recall 96V-088 was done on your car. The fix is free.

issues.t: Ignition switch housing cracks (recall)
issues.sym: After starting, the key does not spring back to the run position, and items like the wipers, lights, or fan may not work.
issues.why: The plastic switch housing can crack where the return spring is anchored, so the switch does not return properly.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to confirm recalls 00V-317 and 06V-403 were completed. Get it fixed before relying on the car in bad weather or at night.

issues.t: Driver air bag can fire from static electricity (recall)
issues.sym: No warning beforehand. In very dry weather, a static shock when getting in or out could set off the driver air bag.
issues.why: The air bag system could be triggered by a static discharge in low humidity.
issues.next: Have a dealer confirm recall 97V-175 was done before driving the car regularly.

issues.t: Rear seat belts may not lock (recall)
issues.sym: A rear seat belt pulls out freely during a hard stop or does not stay locked.
issues.why: The rear belt retractors on some cars could fail to lock or could unlock after locking.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check recall 97V-115, especially if you carry passengers or child seats in back.

issues.t: Weak brake assist in cold weather (recall)
issues.sym: A hard brake pedal and longer stops, mostly on cold days.
issues.why: A vacuum control valve for the brake booster could stick in the cold and cut the vacuum the booster needs.
issues.next: If the pedal feels hard, drive gently and have recall 99V-131 checked by a dealer right away.

issues.t: Throttle may not return to idle after a backfire (recall)
issues.sym: After a cold start, the engine may keep revving higher than normal when you lift off the gas.
issues.why: A screen in the air intake could break during a cold-start backfire, and the pieces could stop the throttle from closing.
issues.next: Do not drive if the engine will not return to idle. Have a dealer confirm recall 98V-134 was done.

issues.t: Tie rod end seals fail (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking over bumps, loose or wandering steering, or uneven front tire wear.
issues.why: The rubber seals on the tie rod ends could split, letting dirt and water wear out the joint inside.
issues.next: Have the tie rods inspected and ask a dealer about recalls 99V-248 and 00V-414.

issues.t: Oil sludge in the 1.8T engine
issues.sym: An oil pressure warning, ticking or knocking noises, or sudden engine damage on a car that seemed fine.
issues.why: The small oil supply and turbo heat break down oil quickly. With long change intervals or the wrong oil, sludge builds up and can block the oil pickup.
issues.next: Stop the engine if the oil light comes on. Use the full synthetic oil Audi specifies, change it often, and have the pickup screen checked on a car with unknown history.

issues.t: Ignition coil failures
issues.sym: A flashing or steady check engine light, misfires, shaking at idle, and rough cold starts.
issues.why: The individual coils that sit on top of each spark plug wear out from heat. When one fails, others often follow.
issues.next: Have misfire codes read soon. Many owners replace all coils and the spark plugs together. A flashing check engine light means ease off and get it in quickly.

issues.t: Crankcase ventilation (PCV) valve and hoses fail
issues.sym: Rough idle, whistling from the engine, lean-running codes, higher oil use, or puffs of blue smoke under hard acceleration.
issues.why: Heat makes the PCV valve and its rubber hoses crack or tear, creating a vacuum leak and letting crankcase pressure push oil where it should not go.
issues.next: Have the PCV system smoke-tested and the failed parts replaced. It is a common and fairly simple repair.

issues.t: Multitronic CVT failure on front-drive models
issues.sym: Jerking or shudder when pulling away, hesitation, slipping, rolling back on hills, or the gear display flashing and the car going into limp mode.
issues.why: The continuously variable transmission used on front-wheel-drive A4s can develop clutch and control unit faults, especially at higher mileage.
issues.next: Have early shudder checked by an Audi specialist. A fluid service and software can help; a failing unit may need its control module or a rebuild. Avoid long trips if the display flashes.

issues.t: Fuel pump can quit and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls while driving or will not restart.
issues.why: A change to a part inside the fuel pump motor could make the pump fail without warning.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to confirm recalls 06V-017 and 07V-375 were completed. A stall in traffic is dangerous, so do not put this off.

issues.t: Xenon headlights dim over time (recall)
issues.sym: The xenon headlights get noticeably dimmer, making night driving harder.
issues.why: A coating inside the headlamp could break down over time and reduce light output.
issues.next: Have a dealer check recall 05V-096 for your car.

issues.t: Camshaft lobe and cam follower wear
issues.sym: Fuel pressure or misfire codes, a check engine light, hesitation, and loss of power.
issues.why: The small follower that drives the high-pressure fuel pump wears through, and the camshaft lobe under it then wears down.
issues.next: Have the cam follower inspected at regular intervals and replaced when worn. Catching it early saves the camshaft and fuel pump.

issues.t: Air bag control unit can corrode (recall)
issues.sym: The air bag warning light comes on. In a crash, the air bags may not deploy.
issues.why: The air bag control unit could corrode and stop working.
issues.next: Do not ignore an air bag light. Have a dealer confirm recall 16V-376 was completed.

issues.t: Excessive oil consumption
issues.sym: Low oil warnings between changes, needing to add oil often, and sometimes blue smoke or fouled spark plugs.
issues.why: The piston rings on early versions of this engine could clog and let oil burn in the cylinders. Audi later changed the pistons.
issues.next: Check the oil at every fill-up and never run it low. Ask an Audi dealer for an oil consumption test and whether any coverage applies.

issues.t: Timing chain tensioner failure
issues.sym: A rattle for a few seconds at cold start that gets worse over time, sometimes with a check engine light.
issues.why: The original tensioner could lose pressure, letting the timing chain go slack and jump a tooth, which can wreck the valves.
issues.next: Have any startup rattle checked right away and do not keep driving on it. An updated tensioner is available.

issues.t: Water pump and thermostat housing leaks
issues.sym: A sweet coolant smell, a low coolant warning, pink or white crust around the engine, or a drip under the car.
issues.why: The water pump and thermostat sit in a plastic housing that warps or cracks after many heat cycles.
issues.next: Top up with the correct Audi coolant and have the leak fixed soon. Stop driving if the temperature warning comes on.

issues.t: Electric after-run coolant pump can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: A coolant or overheating warning, a burning smell from the engine bay, or the pump running loudly after shutoff.
issues.why: Debris in the coolant can jam the small electric pump that circulates coolant after the engine is off. A jammed pump can short circuit and overheat, creating a fire risk.
issues.next: Park outdoors until a dealer confirms recall 18V-229 is done. Get it checked right away if you smell burning.

issues.t: Steering becomes stiff or sticks
issues.sym: The steering suddenly feels heavy, notchy, or stuck, sometimes with a steering fault message.
issues.why: Owners and dealers have traced it to a failing power steering assist unit or a worn intermediate steering shaft.
issues.next: Stop driving if steering becomes hard to turn and have it towed to a dealer. Do not wait for it to happen on the highway.

issues.t: Passenger air bag may switch off (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger air bag off light stays on with an adult in the seat, or an air bag warning appears.
issues.why: A fault in the seat heater wiring can confuse the sensor that detects a front passenger, so the air bag may be turned off.
issues.next: Have a dealer confirm recall 21V-874 was completed. Until then, avoid seating adults up front if the air bag off light is on.

issues.t: Rear trailing arm nut can crack (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or knock from the rear, the car pulling or wandering, or uneven rear tire wear.
issues.why: A lock nut holding the rear trailing arm could crack from stress corrosion and let the arm come loose. A follow-up recall covered alignment checks after the repair.
issues.next: Have a dealer confirm recalls 21V-295 and 22V-034 were done. Stop driving if the rear end feels loose.

issues.t: Rear seat belts may unlock too early (recall)
issues.sym: A child seat secured with a rear seat belt feels loose or the belt does not stay locked.
issues.why: The rear belt retractors could switch out of their child-seat locking mode too soon.
issues.next: Have a dealer check recall 21V-606 before using a belt-installed child seat.

issues.t: Rearview camera shows a blank screen (recall)
issues.sym: The screen stays black or frozen when you shift into reverse.
issues.why: Software errors in the infotainment and camera system could stop the camera image from showing, and on some 2022 cars the unit could be damaged at shutoff.
issues.next: Back up with extra care using your mirrors, and have a dealer apply recalls 21V-825, 22V-742 and 22V-806 as they apply to your car.

issues.t: Engine can stall from a faulty engine computer (recall)
issues.sym: The engine shuts off while driving, often with warning lights, and may not restart.
issues.why: A part inside the engine control unit could short circuit.
issues.next: Have a dealer confirm recall 22V-368 was completed. A stall in traffic is dangerous.

issues.t: Driver air bag inflator can rupture or inflate weakly (recalls)
issues.sym: No warning while driving; the danger shows up only when the air bag fires.
issues.why: Moisture can get into the original driver air bag inflator, so it may burst and throw metal pieces or inflate too little to protect you.
issues.next: Check your VIN and have the inflator replaced before driving it much more; the replacement is free under recall.

issues.t: Aftermarket water pump pulley can crack and take out the timing belt
issues.sym: A rattle or grinding at the front of the engine, coolant loss, then the engine quits and will not restart.
issues.why: One brand of replacement water pump used a pulley that can crack; when it breaks up it throws the timing belt, and these engines bend valves when the belt goes.
issues.next: If a non-original water pump was fitted at a belt service, have the brand checked right away; a thrown belt here means major engine damage.

issues.t: Whistle from the turbo at steady throttle
issues.sym: A thin, steady whistle from under the hood when you hold light to moderate throttle at roughly fifteen hundred to two thousand rpm. It fades when you lift off.
issues.why: Air moving past the turbocharger's recirculation valve sets up a resonance. Audi has a bulletin for the noise with an updated valve and extra sound deadening.
issues.next: Monitor it, as the engine is not being harmed. Mention the bulletin at a normal service visit so nobody starts replacing turbo parts on guesswork.

issues.t: Low coolant message with the level actually correct
issues.sym: A low coolant warning appears on the display even though the reservoir reads full, sometimes together with a stored fault for the radiator shutters.
issues.why: Audi has bulletins for a false low coolant warning on these cars, where the level sensor or the active grille shutter circuit reports a fault rather than the engine losing coolant.
issues.next: Get it checked rather than ignored: a shop should confirm the level by eye, pressure test for a real leak, then read the stored faults before changing parts.

issues.t: Gearbox warning with limp mode or no reverse
issues.sym: A gearbox malfunction message comes up, the car holds itself in one or two gears, or reverse will not engage when you need it.
issues.why: Audi has several bulletins for faults stored in the transmission control module of the twin-clutch gearbox; when it sees a signal it cannot trust, it drops into a protection mode.
issues.next: Have it read quickly and avoid long trips in the meantime, because a car stuck without reverse or in one gear can leave you blocking traffic.

issues.t: Shudder or binding in tight turns on quattro models
issues.sym: At parking speeds with the wheel near full lock the car shudders, hops or feels like the driveline is fighting itself.
issues.why: On the part-time quattro system the clutch that feeds the rear wheels can stay partly engaged when it should release. Audi has returned to the complaint in a run of bulletins.
issues.next: Have the rear axle clutch and its software checked; sorting it early is cheaper than letting the driveline wear.

issues.t: Will not start after sitting from a flat battery
issues.sym: Left parked for a few days the car cranks slowly or not at all, and a string of warning messages shows up once it finally runs.
issues.why: Audi has bulletins on drained twelve volt batteries on these cars and on the mild hybrid system putting itself into low voltage protection, either of which can leave the car unable to start.
issues.next: Have the battery load tested and the drain measured before anyone just fits a new battery, and ask for the mild hybrid system's stored faults to be read too.
